title: local_signal_event
description: One line of signals.jsonl (SignalValue), windows.jsonl (WindowStat), requests.jsonl (AdaptationRequest) context.jsonl (ContextEvent) or frames.jsonl (FrameLog: one line per processed frame). An invalid value is never written as a number: value is null and valid is false. An adaptation request is evidence for the decision layer; it is not a retraining decision.

version.description: signal implementation version (consistency: cell name and package commit)

invalid_reason.description: why the value is invalid, e.g. EMPTY_PAIR, no_boxes, no_features, no_reference, backbone_mismatch

t.description: stream time in seconds (time of the second frame for a pair)

reference_id.description: hash id of the reference bundle used, null for signals without a reference

extras.description: signal-specific fields; consistency: alarm, status, G, G_mc, dx, dy, K, N_t, N_t1; platform_motion: dx, dy, abs_dx, abs_dy, status; confidence: n_boxes; feature_drift: bn_stats_match

statistic.description: aggregate of the valid values of the window; null if too few are valid

change.description: degradation against the reference period: > 0 means worse (difference or ratio form)

window_seconds.description: window length in seconds (window_transitions / frame rate), when the frame rate is known

comparisons.description: every registered comparator of this signal (the signal's own and those requested by trigger rules): key -> {reference, change, reason}

kind.description: replay only: the clip changed; no pair is formed across it

stage.description: screening = an early, sensitive rule (step); confirmation = a rule that needs more evidence (rate, sustained)

rule.description: name of the rule that fired (e.g. step, sustained, rate); every rule that fires emits its own request

comparator.description: reference period the drop is measured against (for a rate rule: the flag condition's comparator)

statistic_before.description: the reference period's level (previous window / anchor)

drop.description: degradation, > 0 = worse (difference or ratio form, see drop_kind)

delta.description: threshold of the drop (for a rate rule: the flag condition's delta)

p_value.description: empirical p-value of the drop against the healthy change distribution that delta was derived from: (1 + #healthy drops >= this drop) / (n + 1); null if no distribution is configured

flag_rate.description: over the last evidence windows: windows, flagged (windows whose flag condition held), rate, healthy_flag_probability (share of healthy windows that would be flagged) and binomial_p (P(at least this many flags | healthy))

context.description: latest window statistic and latest value of every measured signal other than the firing one (e.g. confidence, feature_drift, platform_motion). Context only: no rule reads it.

p_value_floor.description: smallest possible p-value, 1 / (n_healthy + 1); a p-value equal to it means the drop is at least as large as every healthy drop, so p cannot say how much larger

robust_z.description: drop / (1.4826 x MAD of the healthy change distribution): the size of the drop in robust standard deviations of healthy changes; unlike p it does not saturate

video.description: video input: the video the request was raised in (the window's last frame); null for image input

frame_index.description: video input: ORIGINAL frame index (0-based decode order) of that frame; null for image input

frame_id.description: images: the file stem; videos: <video>@<original frame index, 7 digits>

t.description: stream time in seconds (index of the processed frame / effective fps)

frame_index.description: ORIGINAL frame index in the video
